subject: Streamline Payments — simultaneous US/EU edge 502-503 bursts; proposed mitigations and exec note
messages:
From: Tim Fox <tim@streamline-payments.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Mercer <alex@streamline-payments.com>, Streamline SRE <sre@streamline-payments.com>
Date: 2024-08-15T08:12:00Z
Subject: Re: production - large # of 502/503s across US + EU since ~07:50

Neha —

We started seeing a sharp uptick in 502/503 and timeouts across both our US and EU regional traffic starting ~07:50 local. Latency is up (median 600ms -> 1.5s) and our client telemetry shows an order-of-magnitude increase in retries which is amplifying load.

Attached are the traces we captured and a short list of affected endpoints. We switched to a smaller concurrency target on our side but still see errors. Can Redwood confirm whether there was a config change or rollout this morning? This is impacting checkout flows for ~14% of our traffic.

Att: streamline-request-traces-0815.txt

-Tim
Tim Fox
Head of Platform, Streamline Payments
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Tim Fox <tim@streamline-payments.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2024-08-15T08:20:00Z
Subject: Re: production - large # of 502/503s across US + EU since ~07:50

Tim — thanks for the traces and the heads-up. I'm escalating to SRE and accounts immediately.

Planned immediate actions (initial):
- SRE will look for ingress/backing pool saturation and recent control-plane pushes.
- We'll check routing policies that could have caused fanout to saturated pools.
- We will stand up a cross-functional bridge and propose short-term mitigations (regional routing changes / fallback model).

Grace / Marcus / Sean: please react in-thread with findings and proposed containment steps. I'd like an update within 30 mins and a proposed customer-facing message.

Neha Kapoor
Sr. Manager, Customer Reliability (Redwood Inference)
neha@redwood.com
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Tim Fox <tim@streamline-payments.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2024-08-15T08:45:00Z
Subject: RE: production - large # of 502/503s across US + EU since ~07:50

On Thu, Aug 15, 2024 at 08:12 Tim Fox <tim@streamline-payments.com> wrote:
> Neha —
> We started seeing a sharp uptick...

Initial SRE findings:
- Ingress LB (us-east-1 + eu-west-1) shows elevated 5xx originating from connection rejections to backend serving pools; the error profile is consistent with upstream connection saturation and client retry amplification.
- A control-plane partial rollout (config: ingress-proxy affinity adjustments) at 07:36UTC touched routing shards for both regions; we see correlation with error onset.
- KV cache hit rates remain normal; not seeing model-side OOMs.

Proposed containment (short window):
1) Abort/roll back the 07:36 config push for ingress-affinity (immediate).
2) Temporarily route Streamline's critical routes to dedicated pool (if they consent) or to a less-loaded region via geo-failover.
3) Apply a soft circuit-breaker on the affected routes: reduce max concurrent connections to 4 and increase upstream timeout to 35s to avoid fast retry amplification.

I've attached a snapshot of ingress metrics we pulled. We'll start the rollback now and report back in 15–20 minutes.

Att: edge-ingress-metrics-08-15.png

Grace O'Connor
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Fox <tim@streamline-payments.com>, Alex Mercer <alex@streamline-payments.com>
Date: 2024-08-15T09:01:00Z
Subject: Re: production - large # of 502/503s across US + EU since ~07:50

Team —

Thanks for the quick triage. Two asks from my side:
- Exec awareness: I'll surface a one-paragraph incident summary to our CRO + account exec. We should also prep a short note for Streamline's leadership acknowledging impact and proposed compensation options.
- Schedule: let's have a 30-minute bridge at 11:00 UTC for customer + SRE + account team.

I support the rollback and paused rollout. If rollback doesn't reduce errors within 20 minutes, we should failover Streamline's traffic to dedicated capacity for stability; Marcus, can you confirm capacity/latency for their dedicated pool?

Sean Gallagher
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Fox <tim@streamline-payments.com>
Date: 2024-08-15T09:25:00Z
Subject: Re: production - large # of 502/503s across US + EU since ~07:50

Quick mitigation plan (actionable checklist):
1) Roll back ingress affinity config (Grace: in progress).
2) If rollback insufficient, shift Streamline's production route to their reserved dedicated pool (we have headroom for an additional 20% throughput in US; EU will require a small scale-up which we can perform with a 10–15 minute window).
3) Implement rate-limiter and token-bucket on the affected routes (burst=200, refill=50/s) to protect upstream.
4) Deploy an emergency circuit-breaker rule (trip after 5 consecutive 5xx per route, cooldown 60s).
5) Prepare draft customer message (short, transparent, include ETA and remediation steps).

Operational notes: we will also capture pcap-level traces for the affected shards and attach to the incident JIRA (SUP-2183). PagerDuty incident PD-112233 is active.

I will start the dedicated-pool switch steps after rollback validation; estimate 8–12 mins for US, 12–20 mins for EU.

Marcus Lin
Senior Product Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Tim Fox <tim@streamline-payments.com>, Alex Mercer <alex@streamline-payments.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2024-08-15T12:34:00Z
Subject: RE: Streamline Payments — simultaneous US/EU edge 502-503 bursts; proposed mitigations and exec note

Tim / Alex —

Summary & next steps (customer-facing):
- What happened (high-level): a control-plane config rollout changed ingress affinity across multiple shards and coincided with a surge of client retries; that combination amplified load and caused upstream connection rejections manifesting as 502/503.
- What we did (today): rolled back the 07:36 rollout (08:55 UTC), applied temporary circuit-breakers and rate-limiting, and shifted Streamline's critical routes to dedicated capacity in US (completed 09:15 UTC). EU scale-up completed 09:40 UTC.
- Current status: error rate for Streamline traffic is down to baseline (5xx < 0.3%) and latency has returned close to normal. We continue increased monitoring for 48 hours.
- Asks/next steps: please confirm if you want us to keep traffic on dedicated pool for 24–72 hours while we finish the postmortem. We will prepare a concise exec note and propose SLA credit options; Sean to coordinate.

Attachments: postmortem-draft-link.txt (internal draft), edge-ingress-metrics-08-15.png, streamline-request-traces-0815.txt

We will follow up with the bridge notes and the full postmortem when available. Apologies again for the disruption — we know this was customer-impacting and are treating priority accordingly.

Neha Kapoor
Sr. Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com
